frontend/apps/mobile/src/onboarding/FeedbackManager.ts:139 getDrafts() does `return stored ? JSON.parse(stored) : [];` with NO try/catch. A corrupt or truncated FEEDBACK_DRAFTS_KEY value in AsyncStorage (e.g. an interrupted write, storage corruption, or a stale value from an older schema) makes JSON.parse throw synchronously, so the whole getDrafts() promise rejects and the feedback-draft UI that awaits it crashes instead of degrading to an empty list.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/onboarding/FeedbackManager.ts:229 getPendingFeedback() has the identical unguarded pattern `return stored ? JSON.parse(stored) : [];` against PENDING_FEEDBACK_KEY. getPendingFeedback feeds the pending-feedback sync/flush path, so a single corrupt entry throws and blocks ALL queued feedback from ever syncing (no isolation, no self-heal).

This is the SAME class of bug the team already fixed elsewhere in this segment: the prior open finding code-review-mobile-rn-widget-provider-json-parse flagged WidgetDataProvider.getAllWidgetConfigs() for the exact `return stored ? JSON.parse(stored)...` anti-pattern, and the hardened modules in this app (layoutCache.readCachedLayout L22-27, TourManager.loadState L277, HelpCenter.loadUserVotes L191) all wrap the parse in try/catch and drop/ignore the bad value. FeedbackManager was missed.

Fix vector: wrap each JSON.parse in try/catch returning [] on failure (and ideally AsyncStorage.removeItem the corrupt key, matching layoutCache). Beyond the throw, the parsed value is also returned untyped (no cast, no shape guard) so a wrong-shape-but-valid-JSON blob would propagate malformed drafts/submissions downstream. Confidence medium: the missing guard and the throwing path are certain by static read; not upgraded to high because triggering it requires already-corrupt local storage, not normal input.
expert: frontend

frontend/apps/mobile/src/qrcode/QRCodeScanner.ts:368 getScanHistory() does `return stored ? JSON.parse(stored) : [];` against SCAN_HISTORY_KEY with NO try/catch — the same unguarded-persisted-parse anti-pattern as FeedbackManager above.

Blast radius is wider than a read-only getter because getScanHistory() is also on the WRITE path: saveScanToHistory() (frontend/apps/mobile/src/qrcode/QRCodeScanner.ts:345 `const history = await getScanHistory();`) calls it before appending a new entry. So if SCAN_HISTORY_KEY is corrupt, scanning a fresh QR code throws inside saveScanToHistory and the post-scan success handler crashes — not just the history-list screen. (This is distinct from parsePPTPayload at L138, which IS correctly try-caught.)

Note the asymmetry: the parse of UNTRUSTED scanned QR payload (parsePPTPayload, L136-142) is defensively wrapped, but the parse of the app's OWN persisted history — which can still be corrupted by a partial write or OS-level storage issue — is not. Both should be guarded.

Fix vector: wrap JSON.parse in try/catch returning [] (and remove the corrupt key), so a bad history blob self-heals on the next scan instead of blocking all future scans. Confidence medium: throwing path certain by static read; requires already-corrupt storage to trigger.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/price_map.rs:226 get_price_map is the handler for the PUBLIC, UNAUTHENTICATED GET /api/v1/price-map (mounted bare at main.rs:515 `.nest("/api/v1/price-map", routes::price_map::router())`, router() at price_map.rs:174 attaches no auth/throttle layer).

reality-server has NO global per-IP rate-limit layer: the only abuse control (state.inquiry_rate_limiters) is invoked INSIDE the anonymous inquiry (routes/inquiries.rs enforce_inquiry_rate_limit) and report (routes/reports.rs enforce_public_report_rate_limit) POST handlers. The main.rs layer stack (L521-575: DefaultBodyLimit, security_headers, TraceLayer, CorsLayer, host_tenant_middleware) adds no request-rate throttle. So the price-map GET is reachable unthrottled.

On every cache MISS it runs an expensive double-CTE aggregation over `listings` (price_map.rs:253-330): current_period + prior_period, each a full `AVG(CASE WHEN size_sqm>0 THEN price/size_sqm END) ... GROUP BY city` scan. The cache_key (price_map.rs:253-259) is `"{mode}:{time_window}:{property_type}:{city}"` and embeds the RAW free-text `query.city` (L258) — an attacker rotating `?city=a1`, `?city=a2`, ... forces a guaranteed cache miss every request, so each request re-runs both aggregations against the DB.

The BoundedCache (MAX_PRICE_MAP_CACHE_ENTRIES=10_000 with LRU/insertion-order eviction, price_map.rs:57/142) bounds only MEMORY under a distinct-key flood (the existing #3132 tests confirm the OOM guard). It does NOT throttle the per-miss DB aggregation, and the LRU eviction means a distinct-key flood also evicts all legitimately-cached aggregations, collapsing the hit rate and the 1h cache benefit for real visitors. Net effect: an unauthenticated single-IP caller can impose repeated expensive GROUP BY load on the shared public DB pool and bust the cache for everyone.

Fix vector: add a per-IP throttle to the price-map GET (reuse the existing TenantRateLimiterSet / client_ip_bucket primitive already used for inquiries/reports), and/or reduce cache-miss amplification by validating+canonicalising `city` (trim/lowercase/known-city allowlist) before it enters cache_key so arbitrary free-text can't mint unbounded distinct keys. Confidence medium: the absent throttle layer and per-miss aggregation are certain by static read; 'medium' (not high) because the DB cost per aggregation was not runtime-measured from this cloud runner.
expert: rust

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/integrations/install.rs:1675-1687 (create portal connection handler) — base_url = std::env::var("API_BASE_URL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "https://api.ppt.example.com".to_string()), then webhook_url = format!("{}/api/v1/integrations/webhooks/portal/{}", base_url, connection_id) is returned in the 201 PortalConnectionResponse and published to the external portal provider (sreality/bezrealitky/immowelt/custom) as the endpoint they must POST webhooks to. If API_BASE_URL is unset or misconfigured in ANY environment, every portal install silently hands out a webhook URL on the placeholder/example domain api.ppt.example.com — an operator-unowned host. Consequences: (a) inbound portal webhooks never reach api-server (integration silently broken, no error surfaced to the installer); (b) api.ppt.example.com is registerable by a third party, so a misconfigured deploy could direct real portal webhook deliveries — which the portal_webhooks receiver expects to carry HMAC-signed, tenant-scoped payloads — to an attacker-controllable endpoint. Should fail closed (reject/500 CONFIG_ERROR) when API_BASE_URL is unset rather than defaulting to an example domain, mirroring the fail-closed secret handling already used for the *_WEBHOOK_SECRET env vars (portal_webhooks.rs get_portal_webhook_secret, #2263).

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/voice.rs:189-197 (exchange_voice_oauth_tokens) — redirect_uri is read via std::env::var("ALEXA_REDIRECT_URI") / std::env::var("GOOGLE_VOICE_REDIRECT_URI").unwrap_or_else(|_| "https://ppt.three-two-bit.com/api/v1/webhooks/voice/oauth/callback".to_string()), hardcoding the production host as the fallback. The OAuth spec requires the redirect_uri sent in the code->token exchange (oauth_manager.exchange_code at :200) to byte-match the one used in the authorize step. On any non-prod environment (staging / worktree *.dev / local) where the platform-specific REDIRECT_URI env var is not set, the exchange falls back to the prod URI, so it mismatches the authorize-step URI and the provider rejects the exchange — voice-device OAuth linking silently fails on every non-prod deploy with only a generic OAUTH_EXCHANGE_FAILED surfaced. Should derive the fallback from the same API_BASE_URL/host config the rest of the server uses, or fail closed when unset, rather than baking in ppt.three-two-bit.com.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:94-101 — buildWebSocketUrl() appends the raw JWT to the handshake URL as a query parameter: `url.searchParams.set('token', token)`, producing e.g. wss://host/ws?token=<jwt>. The file documents this as an intentional browser constraint (lines 86-92: browsers cannot set an Authorization header on a WebSocket handshake, so the api-server reads the JWT from the `token` query param), so this is a known-tradeoff hardening item, not an undocumented bug.

Residual risk the comment does not address: full request URLs (including the query string) are routinely captured by reverse-proxy / load-balancer / CDN access logs and APM traces, and can surface in browser history — so a long-lived bearer JWT in the WS URL has a wider exposure surface than a header-borne token. Standard mitigation is a dedicated short-lived, single-use WS connect ticket (issued by a POST, valid seconds, exchanged for the socket) or sending the JWT in the first post-connect WS frame rather than the handshake URL.

Low severity / for triage: this is a defense-in-depth suggestion on an explicitly documented design that the api-server currently depends on; changing it requires a coordinated server change, so it is backlog-worthy only if WS access logs are retained with query strings. Flagged for a human to confirm the proxy/log posture before investing. Confidence medium (static read of the documented design; log-retention posture not verified).

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/admin/agencies.rs:185-189 (suspend_organization handler) — after the org is suspended, the code fetches org member user IDs to revoke their sessions: `let user_ids = state.platform_admin_repo.get_org_member_user_ids(id).await.unwrap_or_default();` then loops revoking each user's tokens. If the member-fetch query fails, user_ids is empty, the loop body never runs, and NO member sessions are revoked, with zero trace in logs. The four SSO/session methods should adopt the same runCatching-with-HTTP-status-fallback pattern.
